newsitem.title: USA: Lott again urges White House response on budget.
newsitem.headline: Lott again urges White House response on budget.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott on Thursday repeated a Republican call for the White House to respond to criticism of President Clinton's budget.

Lott, who earlier Thursday sharply criticized Clinton's budget plan, made more conciliatory remarks in a speech to a meeting of the National Conference of State Legislatures, saying he was still committed to working with the President.
"This is not my president (but) I have an obligation to work with him," Lott, a Mississippi Republican, said. "I'm going to do that."
Lott said he had communicated with the White House earlier Thursday and urged them to make a policy response rather than a political response to comments he made at a news conference the same day.
"Show us what we can do to get a balanced budget," Lott said he told the White House, again saying that Clinton should take the lead in the budget negotiations.

He also said he urged the White House to "step up and embrace this consumer price issue." Lott, who has proposed a commission to study shortcomings in the Consumer Price Index, said it would be very difficult to reach a balanced budget without addressing the issue.

At his news conference earlier Thursday, Lott said that if no progress was achieved in negotiations with the White House in the next two weeks he doubted whether an agreement to balance the budget by 2002 could be reached.
